title: Carnival parades and flutes in Pass Christian
summary: Pass Christian had Mardi Gras floats and parades; Handy and his father and brothers played up and down the streets, and the father bought the boys instruments.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: And you came here in 1927. I wonder if there's anything else you could tell us about the music over in Pastor Christian, any of the, uh, bands. Were there any, uh, parade bands on the street?

Well, well, well, well, we had, we had, uh, one of the best, uh, parades. It was, I imagine, during the time that we had parades here, we had them in Pastor Christian. And we had some very, very wonderful flutes. Is that at Mardi Gras time? Mardi Gras times. Albert Alexander had flutes. He sat down and built flutes during the time that we have here today. And I guess that was in 1919 or 1902. We had regular carnival there just like we have here, floats and alls, and we had carnival there. And we was playing up and down the streets for the floats at that time. Well, my father and I and my brothers, my baby brother also, he was a guitar player from Boise. We was all musicians from Boise. Not at all. We had just a glorious time in Paschristian. Only time we had floats in. We never had any floats in Gulfport, Biloxel, Basel, Louis, just in Paschristian. Uh-huh. And we had glorious time there, just with floats. Well, after years that passed, well, this fella by name, my father bought all of us instruments, all kind of instruments, porcelain. Well, John, he learned clarinet and saxophone. Me, I learned bass violin. My baby brother, he learned guitar.
